To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
soil enzyme activities can be used as an indicator of soil quality.
no tillage planting causes significant improvement of soil quality, and the use of manuring is more effective than the use of mineral fertilization in the maintenance of soil fertility.

soil enzymatic activities are influenced by the crop rotation, tillage and fertilization, and that the soil enzymatic activities under maize were significantly lower than those under wheat, while the activities of the soil under farmyard manure were higher than those of the soil under mineral fertilization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of soil management (tillage, crop rotation, fertilization) on soil enzymatic activities.
the influence of tillage, crop rotation and fertilization on soil quality indicators, particularly enzymatic activities, and with the possibility of using them to monitor the soil fertility status.
a complex experiment including no tillage, crop rotation, fertilization and sampling depth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no till and farmyard manured soils were more enzyme active than conventionally tilled soils.
no tillage, 6 crop rotation, and farmyard manured maize are the best soil management options for improving preluvosoil quality.
the no tillage system, combined with farmyard manure application, is a promising practice for sustainable soil management in the preluvosoil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
no tillage in comparison with conventional soil cultivation resulted in a significant increase in the soil enzymatic activities, which is a good indicator of soil fertility and quality.

soil enzymatic activities are sensitive indicators of soil management and can be used for evaluation of the soil potential to function in nutrient cycling processes and for the assessment of the sustainability of agricultural management.
the enzymatic activities were higher in the 6 crop than in the 1 2 crop rotation and higher in the no tillage than in the conventional tillage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
no tillage and farmyard manure are the most important factors for improving the soil quality.

soil management can affect soil enzymatic activities and that the use of soil enzymes in soil quality assessments may provide useful information on the potential of soils to perform processes such as decomposition and mineralization.
the use of no tillage and farmyard manure in combination with 6 crop rotations may be a good strategy to maintain and/or improve the soil quality of preluvosoil.
